title: a retry hop the broker refuses requeues only that delivery, and the consumer carries on
comment: Java closed the channel, sending every in-flight delivery back and stopping the consumer; Ruby left the delivery unacknowledged for the life of the channel.
The broker refuses the hop through a reject-publish policy on the source queue and its rungs, applied once the five messages are in and before the first retry's wait is over.
Prefetch 2 keeps m1 and m2 in flight and m3..m5 ready, so the queue is over its limit of zero when the hop is attempted, for quorum queues as well as classic ones.

m1 coming back with the redelivered flag set is the broker's own evidence that it was requeued rather than republished; m2 never being redelivered is the evidence that nothing else was settled with it.

steps.comment: the hop is attempted at about 5s and refused
